body.statement: Does \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{CR}}<\rho_n^W\) hold for every even \(n\ge10\)? Derive either a legal all-size family of full-count perturbations and matching active-state inequalities, or an explicit later even counterexample with a scalar saddle certificate. The derivation must control every new response-type state and cannot infer persistence from the \(n=8\) witness alone.
body.justification: Strictness need not propagate because padding changes allocation mixtures, the feasible state lattice, and least-favorable supports.
body.gap: Hull states a related general complete-randomization conjecture, while no located source gives the required uniform separating-prior or active-gradient argument for this compression comparison.
body.consumer: A resolution would determine whether software should preserve the second count at every larger balanced binary experiment or only at selected sizes.
